title: Lighthouse Historical Record
description: Canonical schema for Lighthouse historical knowledge-base records. Covers two record types: problem_statement and project. Every record carries provenance, licence, and field-level verification metadata. Schema version 1.0.0.

verification_status.description: Provenance status of a field value. 'verified' = confirmed from primary source. 'inferred' = derived from secondary evidence. 'unverified' = present but not checked. 'unknown' = no information available.

licence_status.description: High-level redistribution assessment. 'unknown' MUST be used when licence information is not available. Do NOT default to 'open'.

provenance.description: Source attribution and access metadata for the record.

source_url.description: The URL from which the record was obtained.

publisher.description: Name of the platform, organisation or individual that published the source material.

access_date.description: ISO 8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD) when the source was accessed.

licence_identifier.description: SPDX licence identifier, URL, or free-text name of the licence. Null when licence is unknown.

redistribution_note.description: Human-readable note about redistribution rights, caveats, or required attribution. Null if not assessed.

outcome.description: Documented outcome of a historical project. Only include when evidence exists; never fabricate outcomes.

summary.description: Brief factual description of the project outcome.

evidence_url.description: URL to evidence supporting the claimed outcome.

ingestion_metadata.description: Metadata about when and how the record entered the Lighthouse dataset.

ingested_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when this record was first ingested.

ingested_by.description: Identifier of the person or automated pipeline that ingested this record.

last_reviewed_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the most recent human review. Null if not yet reviewed.

review_notes.description: Free-text notes from the most recent review. Null if none.

problem_statement.description: A historical problem statement issued at a hackathon, competition, or challenge.

record_id.description: Stable, globally unique identifier for this problem statement. Prefix: ps-.

title.description: Short title of the problem statement.

description.description: Full text or summary of the problem statement.

event_name.description: Name of the hackathon or competition event.

event_date.description: Date of the event (ISO 8601 YYYY-MM-DD). Null if unknown.

requirements.description: Explicit requirements stated in the problem. Null if not documented.

constraints.description: Explicit constraints stated in the problem. Null if not documented.

technologies.description: Technologies explicitly mentioned in the problem statement. Null if none documented. Do NOT infer from other sources.

field_verification.description: Per-field verification status for key fields. Allows consumers to distinguish verified facts from inferred or unverified data.

project.description: A historical hackathon or competition project submission.

record_id.description: Stable, globally unique identifier for this project. Prefix: proj-.

description.description: Full text or summary description of the project.

event_name.description: Name of the hackathon or competition.

event_date.description: Date of the event (ISO 8601). Null if unknown.

problem_statement_id.description: Reference to the problem statement this project addressed, if known. Must match a record_id in problem_statements.

requirements.description: Requirements the project aimed to meet. Null if not documented.

constraints.description: Constraints the project operated under. Null if not documented.

technologies.description: Technologies explicitly documented as used in the project. Do NOT infer from repository contents.

team_size.description: Number of team members. Null if not documented.

field_verification.description: Per-field verification status for key fields.

outcomes.description: Documented outcomes. Null if no outcomes are known. NEVER fabricate outcomes.
